fonts.designer: Juliette Duhé, Léa Pradine, Valentin Papon, Chloé Lozano, Sébastien Riollier
fonts.description: Five deliberately distinct styles assembled from different periods of typewriter history.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It behaves like a small historical ensemble rather than a smooth weight family, excellent for documentary hierarchy.

fonts.description: A variable drawing-like family with independent Scribble and Scrabble axes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Two independent roughness systems let the letterforms change behavior instead of merely adding a distressed surface.

fonts.description: A cube-like display alphabet whose stretch, flavor, and slice axes mutate counterforms and switch curves into straight lines.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Three legible conceptual axes make it an unusually good test object for interactive and generative typography.

fonts.description: A variable alphabet connecting counter shape to musical amplitude and frequency.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: The axes map cleanly to sound concepts, making it immediately relevant to browser music systems and performance visuals.

fonts.description: A variable display family controlled by Charge and Power axes, like a typographic device state.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: The axis model communicates a visible system state, a better reason to animate than ambient motion.

fonts.description: A large modular display system with neon, tube, rat, patterned, slanted, and playground constructions.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It is a kit of materially different constructions rather than a single decorative cut.

fonts.description: A Filipino display family assembled in sheet, stripe, and strip variants.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its layered variants connect display typography to woven and cut material logic.

fonts.description: A sharp contemporary serif spanning light through dark weights with matching italics and Cyrillic support.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It supplies a genuinely usable libre editorial family rather than another display-only experiment.

fonts.description: An industrial optical-size system with multiple ink-trap intensities and cuts tuned from caption to very large display.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its optical and production logic makes industrial character functional rather than cosmetic.

fonts.description: A symbolic display alphabet whose glyphs behave like compact creatures, masks, or diagrammatic figures.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It sits between alphabet, pictogram, and character set without becoming a texture effect.

fonts.description: A five-cut optical family moving from caption through banner sizes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its deliberately separate optical cuts make scale comparison meaningful in the lab.

fonts.description: A three-size display family named Chica, Mediana, and Grande with a warm, plantlike silhouette.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its scale-specific drawings provide a compact alternative to one-size display lettering.

fonts.description: A dense ornamental display face with dark, polished shapes and emphatic joins.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It brings severe ornament into the collection without relying on distressed surfaces.

fonts.description: An uppercase painted display alphabet with compact, handmade mass.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its painted construction supplies a direct vernacular counterweight to polished commercial display faces.

fonts.description: A compact industrial family interpolating between compressed and original widths.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its narrow width range produces practical state and density changes without spectacle.

fonts.description: A rounded, organ-like display alphabet with inflated internal forms.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It creates biological atmosphere through letter anatomy rather than visual effects.

fonts.description: A compact irregular display face with lively commercial-lettering rhythm.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It has the energy of everyday commercial ephemera while remaining clean enough to test.

fonts.description: A high-personality serif with calligraphic movement and uneven historical pressure.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It offers literary drama from stroke behavior rather than faux-luxury contrast.

fonts.description: A seven-cut optical display serif tuned from 12 to 96 point settings.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its many optical drawings make it valuable for studying how personality changes with scale.

fonts.description: An adversarial display alphabet built around collision, obstruction, and awkward recognition.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It tests legibility as an active conflict rather than simply distorting clean letters.

fonts.description: A four-weight landscape-oriented display family with broad, expressive silhouettes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its horizontal presence offers a useful compositional contrast to the collection’s condensed faces.

fonts.description: A regional display face with angular, signlike construction and an intentionally local voice.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It adds a place-specific vernacular voice rather than generic international display polish.

fonts.description: A compact two-weight display sans with rigid geometry and abrupt terminals.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its restraint makes it a plausible working component beside stranger faces.

fonts.description: A compact botanical display face named for an orchid genus.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It introduces organic character through proportion and terminals rather than illustration.

fonts.description: A contemporary Insular family combining uncial minuscule, Roman proportion, Fraktur edge, Gaelic stone carving, and Book of Kells references.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It is the strongest Celtic candidate when the project needs historical signal without souvenir-shop decoration.

fonts.description: An Insular text face based on letterforms familiar from older Irish printing, with a less theatrical and more documentary voice.
fonts.languageSupport: Irish, Scottish Gaelic, and Latin-script languages
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It gives the lab an actual reading-oriented Insular form, not just a Celtic display accent.

fonts.description: A runny calligraphic display system that stretches from airy and condensed to dense and wide constructions.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its width interpolation changes texture and gesture, not just line length.

fonts.description: A sharp serif system spanning condensed, regular, and extended widths from thin to black.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: The width-and-weight matrix makes an unusually characterful but usable editorial system.

fonts.description: A high-contrast display serif with an extra-italic construction that feels written, unstable, and formal at once.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its extra italic is a useful atmospheric counterpoint to conventional editorial italics.

fonts.description: A thorny high-contrast serif split into angular and linear constructions.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: The paired constructions let the same sharp voice move between brittle and more readable settings.

fonts.description: A Times-derived serif disrupted by covertly altered joins and proportions.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It is useful for testing how much structural wrongness can hide inside a familiar reading texture.

fonts.description: A soft, heavy display serif with calligraphic bulges and generous dark shapes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It supplies tactile warmth without leaning on polished luxury-serif conventions.

fonts.description: A display family influenced by southern Italian inscriptional and vernacular forms.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its geographic reference feels specific and constructed rather than vaguely classical.

fonts.description: A compact display family with dense joins and eccentric organic silhouettes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It occupies a useful zone between botanical, mechanical, and deliberately awkward.

fonts.description: A width-driven display system with thin and regular cuts across condensed, normal, and expanded forms.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its exaggerated width states are blunt enough to expose layout behavior immediately.

fonts.description: A sparse monospaced face with a dry terminal and early-computer plainness.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It gives the lab a practical mono whose oddness comes from drawing, not screen effects.

fonts.description: A stripped single-weight sans with abrupt, economical forms and visible construction decisions.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It is quiet enough for utility text but refuses the anonymous neutrality of a standard UI sans.

fonts.description: A deliberately rough grotesk with five weights and blunt commercial-print energy.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It can carry interface structure while keeping a visibly human, non-startup texture.

fonts.description: A very wide sans with loud rounded curves, redrawn to survive smaller text sizes.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its extreme width is functional enough to test beyond posters, which makes it a useful layout stressor.

fonts.description: A six-style reinterpretation of Arial that keeps office-software familiarity while shifting its construction and tone.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It turns the most ordinary system-font reference into a consciously redrawn vernacular tool.

fonts.description: A deliberately collective Belgian typographic system preserved in several numbered states.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: Its identity is procedural and collaborative, making iteration itself part of the family.

fonts.designer: Pierre Huyghebaert, Pierre Marchand, Delphine Platteeuw, and Gregoire Vigneron
fonts.description: A scanned and reconstructed Univers Else descendant whose irregularities retain the pressure of its production process.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It makes reproduction history visible without applying a fake damage filter.

fonts.description: Twenty-seven remixed Linux Libertine variations created by copying, substituting, and rotating glyph parts for the FLOSS+Art book.
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It treats a type family as an editorial indexing mechanism rather than a ladder of weights.

fonts.description: A reinterpretation of Nimbus Mono with Cyrillic expansion and private-use ornamental glyphs from OSP workshops.
fonts.licenseName: GNU GPL v2 with font embedding exception
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It is a real open-computing artifact with useful system texture and a documented lineage.

fonts.description: A libre engineering and signage study that includes the OSP-DIN and DIN-Eden constructions.
fonts.languageSupport: Basic Latin with partial extended coverage
fonts.reasonsInteresting: It brings norm-lettering logic into the lab through an actual collaborative reconstruction.
